_meta: Per-check guidance: `fix` is a copy-pasteable code snippet; `verify` lists commands the user can run to manually confirm the issue and to confirm their fix landed.

core_version.title: Suppress WordPress version disclosure

users.title: Block ?author= and REST user enumeration

tls_headers.title: Add baseline security headers (Nginx)

csp.title: Tighter CSP (Apache)
csp.code:
Header set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self' https:; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; base-uri 'self'"
Header set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
Header set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"

exposed_files.title: Block common backup/source-leak paths (Nginx)

plugins.title: Block plugin readme.txt files
plugins.code:
location ~ ^/wp-content/plugins/.+/readme\.txt$ { deny all; }
location ~ ^/wp-content/plugins/.+/readme\.md$ { deny all; }

csp: # Mozilla Observatory grades your overall header config:
subdomains: # Manual takeover check for a suspect subdomain:
waf: # wafw00f gives a more detailed fingerprint:
core_cves: # Compare your installed version to the advisory:
plugin_cves: # List installed plugins and versions (run on the server):
rest_api: # Restrict via rest_endpoints filter in functions.php
cors: # Look at Access-Control-Allow-Origin in the response
secret_leak: # TruffleHog scans web assets for secrets:
login_throttle_deep: # Verify the threshold manually by repeating wrong-password attempts:
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -X POST {target}/wp-login.php -d 'log=fakeuser&pwd=wrong' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n'; sleep 10; done
ajax_surface: # Audit which nopriv handlers your plugins register:
core_tampering: # Compare a suspect file against the same path in a clean WP of your version:
# Or run Wordfence / Sucuri SiteCheck for a full malware sweep
dns_security: # Then harden in your DNS provider — set 'v=spf1 ... -all' and 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:...'
source_maps: # Grep a JS bundle for the trailing comment:
# Fix at the build tool: Webpack `devtool: false` for prod; Vite `build.sourcemap: false`; Next.js `productionBrowserSourceMaps: false`
# Or block at the web server: `location ~ \.map$ { deny all; }`
js_supply_chain: # Look for missing integrity= attributes and unfamiliar hosts.
# Generate an SRI hash for an external script:
curl -s https://cdn.example.com/lib.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A
# Add it to the tag: <script src="..." integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous">
# Polyfill.io / bootcdn.net etc. — REMOVE entirely or self-host.
wp_rest_methods: for ns in wp/v2/posts wp/v2/users wp/v2/comments wp/v2/media contact-form-7/v1 wc/v3; do echo "--- $ns"; curl -sX OPTIONS {target}/wp-json/$ns -i | grep -iE 'allow:|access-control'; done
# Lock down via rest_endpoints filter or rest_authentication_errors in functions.php
# WooCommerce: regenerate API keys at WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API
